 Learn more Arm earnings in focus as investors watch royalties and AI exposure 
 Arm Holdings (NasdaqGS:ARM) heads into its upcoming quarterly report with attention squarely on whether customer commitments are showing up as shipped chips and how royalties stack up against licensing income. 
 Recent trading has been rough for Arm Holdings, with the share price down about 10% in the last session and roughly 33% over 30 days. Even so, the year to date share price return of 79.53% and 3 year total shareholder return of 287.89% still point to strong longer run momentum, so the upcoming earnings update is arriving at a moment when sentiment has cooled and investors are reassessing how much AI exposure and royalty growth they are willing to pay for. 
 Scan beyond Arm Holdings and line up potential beneficiaries or peers with AI exposure using our curated list of 54 AI infrastructure stocks as this earnings season unfolds. 
 Arm Holdings is being pulled between two stories right now: a sharp pullback driven by sector worries, and a business still reporting solid revenue and net income growth. At this price, which one are you really paying for? 
 Most Popular Narrative: 52% Undervalued 
 Arm Holdings last closed at $205.97, while the most followed narrative on the stock pins fair value much higher at $430. The gap investors are debating is whether that valuation framework is realistic or simply too generous for current conditions. 
 The issue is not operating quality. The issue is that the market is capitalizing a large part of the FY2031 dream today. 
 So the thesis is not "Arm is cheap." It is: Arm may be one of the most strategically important companies in computing, but the stock already assumes a very large part of that future. 
 See why 43 investors see Arm Holdings as 52% undervalued . 
 Result: Fair Value of $430 (UNDERVALUED) 
 Still, the Arm Holdings story can break if the AGI CPU stumbles commercially, or if FTC scrutiny and customer pushback reshape how aggressively it can pursue AI silicon. 
 Find out about the key risks to this Arm Holdings narrative . 
 Another View on Arm Holdings: cash flows vs narrative 
 The narrative crowd sees Arm Holdings as 52% undervalued at $430, yet our DCF model tells a very different story. On projected cash flows, the SWS DCF model points to fair value around $92.61, which would frame the current $205.97 share price as clearly overvalued. Which lens do you trust more when the numbers disagree this much?
